blocks.text: I can use ‘j’ai’ and ‘il, elle a’ with nouns to say what I have or he, she has.
Tap each word to see what it means.
Listen, repeat and read the days of the week. Don’t forget: there are no capital letters for days in French!

items: il y a sept jours dans la semaine = There are seven days in the week
lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi = Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday
samedi et dimanche, c’est le week-end = Saturday and Sunday, it’s the weekend

blocks.text: You can revisit the days of the week regularly by listening to a song.

blocks.q: Use the order lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche.

blocks.text: To ask ‘what day is it?’, we can use intonation.
To answer, we could say {aujourd’hui c’est} followed by the day of the week. It means ‘today it’s …’.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: Aujourd’hui just means ‘today’. To say ‘today it is’ you need aujourd’hui c’est.

blocks.q: Which is the correct way to say ‘Today it’s Friday’?
blocks.why: To say ‘today it’s …’ you need aujourd’hui c’est, then the day of the week.

blocks.q: Today is samedi. Someone asks: ‘C’est vendredi ?’ What is the right answer?
blocks.why: Today is samedi, so the answer is no, and we say aujourd’hui c’est samedi.

blocks.text: The verb {avoir} means ‘to have’. {J’ai} means ‘I have’.
Je becomes j’ before a vowel.
{Il a} means ‘he has’. {Elle a} means ‘she has’.

blocks.label: What do you notice?
blocks.text: For a boy you use the pronoun ‘il’ and for a girl you use ‘elle’, but the verb ‘a’ stays the same for both.
We use these verbs with nouns and their indefinite articles (un or une) to say what I and someone else have.

items: J’ai un chien. = I have a dog.
Il a une orange. = He has an orange.
Elle a un chat. = She has a cat.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: You can’t use ‘avoir’ as it is. You must change the verb depending on who you are talking about: j’ai, il a or elle a.

blocks.why: Je becomes j’ before a vowel: j’ai.

blocks.q: Match the French to the English.
Sort the sentences by who has the thing.

items: You can revisit the days of the week regularly by listening to a song.
To ask what day it is, use intonation: c’est lundi ? To answer, use aujourd’hui c’est and the day: non, aujourd’hui c’est mardi.
The verb avoir means ‘to have’. J’ai means ‘I have’, il a means ‘he has’ and elle a means ‘she has’.
We use these verbs with nouns and their indefinite articles to say what I and someone else have.

flashcards.back:
I have

J’ai une table. = I have a table.

he has

Il a un stylo. = He has a pen.

she has

Elle a un sac. = She has a bag.

flashcards.front: Does the verb change between ‘il a’ and ‘elle a’?
flashcards.back: No. Il is for a boy and elle is for a girl, but the verb ‘a’ stays the same.

flashcards.front: What happens to ‘je’ before a vowel?
How many days are there in the week in French?
flashcards.back: Seven: il y a sept jours dans la semaine.

flashcards.front: Which two days are the weekend (le week-end)?
Write the French days of the week in order.
flashcards.back: lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche

flashcards.front: Do days of the week start with a capital letter in French?
flashcards.back: No. In French there are no capital letters for days.

flashcards.front: How do you ask ‘what day is it?’ with intonation?
flashcards.back:
Say a day and raise your voice at the end.

C’est mardi ?

today it’s …

Non, aujourd’hui c’est lundi.

questions.prompt: What does the French verb ‘avoir’ mean in English?
What does ‘j’ai’ mean in English? (two words)
What does ‘il a’ mean in English? (two words)
What does ‘elle a’ mean in English? (two words)
Write the French for ‘I have a pen.’
questions.explanation: J’ai means ‘I have’ and stylo is masculine, so we use un.

questions.prompt: Write the French for ‘He has a bottle.’
questions.explanation: Il a means ‘he has’ and bouteille is feminine, so we use une.

questions.prompt: Write the French for ‘She has a game.’
questions.explanation: Elle a means ‘she has’ and jeu is masculine, so we use un.

questions.prompt: Which French day of the week comes after mardi?
questions.explanation: The order is lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche.

questions.prompt: Which French day of the week comes between jeudi and samedi?
questions.explanation: The order is jeudi, vendredi, samedi.

questions.prompt: In French, which day of the week comes after samedi?
questions.explanation: Samedi and dimanche are the weekend, in that order.

questions.prompt: Write the French for ‘today it’s’ (two words).
questions.explanation: Aujourd’hui means ‘today’, and you need c’est to say ‘today it’s …’.
